73 Local SEO Statistics Every Contractor Should Know [2025 Data]

73 local SEO statistics covering Google Business Profile, reviews, local pack, mobile search, voice search, and ROI. All verified with sources. Updated for...

OnwardCraft Team Growth Strategists

Most local SEO advice is recycled from blog posts written three years ago. The numbers have changed. Consumer behavior has shifted. And AI search has rewritten the rules.

This article gives you 73 verified local SEO statistics — every number sourced, every trend contextualized, every data point actionable for contractors and home service businesses. Whether you're building a case for local SEO investment, benchmarking your performance, or optimizing for the AI search era, these are the numbers that matter.

  3. Reviews and Ratings (Statistics 26–38)

Local Search Behavior (Statistics 1–12)

Local search behavior is the foundation of everything that follows. These 12 statistics show how consumers actually search for local businesses — and what happens after they do.

1. 46% of All Google Searches Have Local Intent

Statistic: Nearly half of all Google searches are looking for something nearby.

Source: Google / BrightLocal

Year: 2025–2026

Context: This number has climbed steadily from 30% in 2019. For contractors, it means almost every search your potential customer makes has local intent baked in. You're not competing with the entire internet — you're competing with the 10–20 businesses in your service area.

2. 80% of U.S. Consumers Search for Local Businesses Weekly

Statistic: Four out of five Americans search for local businesses at least once per week.

Source: BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey

Year: 2026

Context: This isn't occasional behavior. It's habitual. Your customers are searching weekly — and if you're not visible when they do, your competitors are.

3. 32–39% Search Daily for Local Products or Services

Statistic: Roughly one-third of consumers search for local businesses every single day.

Source: BrightLocal / Nielsen

Year: 2026

Context: Daily searchers are typically in active buying mode. For emergency services like plumbing, HVAC, and electrical, daily searchers represent your highest-intent leads.

4. 98% of Customers Search Online for Nearby Companies

Statistic: Virtually every consumer uses online search to find local businesses.

Source: WiserReview

Year: 2025–2026

Context: The 2% who don't are outliers. If your business isn't findable online, you're invisible to 98% of your market.

5. 87% Rely on Google for Local Searches

Statistic: Google dominates local search with nearly 9 in 10 consumers using it as their primary local discovery tool.

Source: WiserReview

Year: 2026

Context: While AI tools are growing (see Statistic 59), Google remains the dominant platform. Your Google Business Profile and local organic presence are still your highest-leverage assets.

6. 76% of "Near Me" Searches Lead to a Store Visit Within 24 Hours

Statistic: Three out of four people who search for something nearby physically visit a business within a day.

Source: Search Engine Land / Digital Applied

Year: 2026

Context: "Near me" searches are purchase-intent signals. For contractors, this translates to service calls — not just website visits. The proximity and immediacy of local search create a direct path from search to revenue.

7. 28–31% of Local Searches Result in a Purchase

Statistic: Nearly one-third of local searches lead directly to a transaction.

Source: Multiple sources

Year: 2026

Context: Compare this to general organic search conversion rates of 2–3%. Local search converts at 10x the rate because the intent is explicit — the searcher needs a service now, in a specific location.

8. 18% of Local Mobile Searches Lead to Purchase Within 24 Hours

Statistic: Nearly 1 in 5 local mobile searches results in a same-day purchase.

Source: AIO SEO

Year: 2025

Context: Mobile local searchers are the most action-oriented segment. They're not researching for next month — they're looking for someone to call right now.

9. 90% of Searchers Buy Within a Week of Their Local Query

Statistic: Nine out of ten local searchers make a purchase within seven days.

Source: WiserReview

Year: 2026

Context: The local search-to-purchase window is compressed. Unlike high-consideration purchases that take months, local services (especially emergency trades) close fast. Your follow-up speed matters more than your nurture sequence.

10. 75% of Businesses Say Local SEO Drives More Leads Than Any Other Channel

Statistic: Three-quarters of businesses report local SEO as their top lead generation channel.

Source: WiserReview

Year: 2026

Context: This isn't theoretical. Businesses running local SEO alongside paid search, social media, and referrals consistently rank local SEO as their highest-ROI channel.

11. 72% of Homeowners Research Contractors Online Before Calling

Statistic: Nearly three-quarters of homeowners do online research before contacting a contractor.

Source: Button Block

Year: 2026

Context: Your website, Google Business Profile, and reviews are your first impression. If they don't like what they see online, they never call.

12. Home Services Local Search Category Grew 33.9% in 2025

Statistic: Home services was the third-fastest-growing local search category, behind only food & beverage (41.2%) and healthcare (37.6%).

Source: Google / Industry Reports

Year: 2025

Context: Demand for home services is surging. More searches mean more opportunity — but also more competition. The contractors who invested in local SEO before this surge are now capturing the overflow.

Statistic: Google Business Profile signals are the #1 ranking factor for the Local Pack, weighted at 32%.

Context: No other factor comes close. Your primary category, profile completeness, posting frequency, and photo uploads collectively determine whether you appear in the 3-Pack more than any backlink or citation ever will.

Statistic: Businesses with fully completed profiles receive seven times more clicks than incomplete profiles.

Source: Google / Decoding

Year: 2025–2026

Context: "Complete" means every field filled: description, services, products, attributes, Q&A, photos, posts, and updates. Most contractors fill out 30% of their profile and wonder why they don't rank.

Statistic: A fully optimized profile nearly triples perceived reputation.

Source: Google

Year: 2025

Context: Trust is the currency of local search. Before a customer ever reads a review or visits your website, your GBP tells them whether you're a legitimate operation or a fly-by-night operator.

16. 70% More Likely to Visit Businesses With a Complete GBP

Statistic: Consumers are 70% more likely to physically visit (or call) a business that has a complete Google Business Profile.

Year: 2025

Source: Google

Year: 2025

Reviews and Ratings (Statistics 26–38)

Statistic: Reviews are the #2 ranking factor for the Local Pack, weighted at 20% (up from ~16% in previous years).

Statistic: Nearly 9 in 10 consumers trust a stranger's online review as much as a recommendation from someone they know.

Context: Twenty reviews is the new minimum viable threshold. Below that, consumers question whether you're established enough to trust. For contractors, this means systematic review generation from day one.

Statistic: Nearly half of all local search clicks go to the Local Pack.

FAQ Section

What percentage of Google searches are local?

46% of all Google searches have local intent, according to Google and BrightLocal data from 2025–2026. This number has grown steadily from 30% in 2019, driven by mobile adoption and voice search.

How many reviews do I need to rank in the Local Pack?

Businesses with 50+ reviews are 266% more likely to appear in the Local Pack than those with fewer reviews. However, review signals include quantity, velocity, recency, and response rate — not just total count. Aim for consistent new reviews (3–5 per week) rather than a one-time push.

What is the ROI of local SEO for contractors?

Local SEO delivers a 680% ROI on average, with service businesses breaking even in 5–6 months. Mature local SEO programs generate leads at $10–$50 per lead — significantly lower than paid search ($45–$228 per lead).

How important is Google Business Profile for local SEO?

GBP signals account for 32% of Local Pack ranking factors — the single largest factor. Complete profiles get 7x more clicks, and verified profiles appear 80% more often in search results.

What percentage of consumers read online reviews?

97% of consumers read online reviews for local businesses, and 88% trust them as much as personal recommendations. Only 3% of consumers skip reviews entirely.

How fast do local SEO leads convert?

76% of local searchers visit a business within 24 hours, and 28–31% of local searches result in a purchase. Mobile local searches convert even faster — 18% lead to a same-day purchase.

Is voice search important for local SEO?

Yes. 76% of voice searches are local in nature, and voice searches are 3x more likely to be local than text searches. As smart speaker adoption grows, voice search optimization is becoming critical for local visibility.

How is AI changing local SEO?

45% of consumers now use ChatGPT or AI tools for local recommendations — up from 6% in 2025. AI Overviews appear on 40.2% of local queries, and visibility in AI recommendations is 30x harder than traditional local search ranking.

What is the minimum star rating consumers will accept?

68% of consumers won't consider a business below 4 stars, and 31% now require 4.5+ stars (up from 17% in 2025). The floor is rising — a 3.8-star rating eliminates you from most consumers' consideration sets.

How often should I post on Google Business Profile?

Businesses posting weekly to GBP see 70% more engagement. Weekly posts signal active management to Google and keep your profile fresh for consumers. Post updates, offers, events, and photos consistently.

What is NAP consistency and why does it matter?

NAP (Name, Address, Phone) consistency means your business information is identical across all directories and platforms. Businesses with 95%+ NAP consistency rank 3.2 positions higher in the local pack. Inconsistent NAP also confuses AI tools — only 68% of AI-generated business info matches GBP data.

How long does it take to see results from local SEO?

Service businesses typically break even in 5–6 months. You may see ranking improvements in 30–90 days, but significant lead volume growth usually takes 6–12 months of consistent optimization.

What is the Local Pack vs. organic results?

The Local Pack is the map with 3 business listings that appears for local-intent searches. It captures 42% of local search clicks and generates 93% more actions than positions 4–10. Organic results appear below the Local Pack and capture the remaining clicks.

Do I need to respond to every review?

Yes. 88% of consumers are more likely to use a business that responds to all reviews, and systematic response improves conversion by 4.1% for every 25% of reviews responded to. Responding to 100% of reviews can deliver a 16%+ conversion lift.

Is local SEO better than paid search for contractors?

Local SEO and paid search serve different purposes. Paid search delivers immediate leads but at higher cost ($45–$228 per lead). Local SEO takes 5–6 months to break even but delivers leads at $10–$50 long-term. The most successful contractors use both — paid search for immediate cash flow, local SEO for sustainable growth.
